sample_scope.scope: Bounded selected long-form YouTube metadata; public first-party documents and separate Hacker News and third-party X evidence.

top10.ranking_basis: Prioritize fresh named events with matched YouTube attention and comparable video observations, then separate audience evidence by originating publisher or community. Broader means two useful families for this bounded sample; limited means one or qualified mixed-program attention. Brief usefulness does not turn into a popularity score.

errors.issue: All ten original YouTube watch requests throttled.
errors.effect: No playback, verified counters, comments, subscribers or disclosures were available.
errors.correction: Preserved tracker timestamp and provenance. Read a complete displayed IBM caption mirror, partial AI Engineer captions and an indexed Y Combinator transcript excerpt; kept counts separate.

errors.issue: Direct X access returned 403; the Gemini Hacker News item returned 429.
errors.effect: X metrics are third-party. Gemini discussion metrics came from the platform day index, with unknown refresh time.
errors.correction: Retained original URLs and separate metric sources. Verified releases using accessible publisher documentation and used distinct evidence families.

errors.issue: Two creator programs cover several events. Arete-27B author page and model-card reads failed.
errors.effect: Roundup views cannot be allocated to a named release. The Arete claim remains underqualified.
errors.correction: Assigned each roundup to one primary discovery event only, kept counts program-level, and held Arete in the editorial watchlist.

errors.issue: Initial local check used the wrong return property name for the reporter freshness field.
errors.effect: First harness assertion failed before any write.
errors.correction: Used the actual report_freshness and report_valid fields and reran with stop-on-error. The pre-write and committed-byte validations both passed.

improvements.change: Program-matched captions and publication-specific original documentation narrowed the technical claims.
Recorded publisher-family removal assessments across ten topics; the prior unified metrics had two recorded.
Try another freely accessible original publisher transcript and a direct timed counter on event-matched non-vendor coverage.

defects: Per-topic article/video/podcast search coverage is incomplete, invalid or bound to a different input.
limitations: The report labels its research partial.
Ten named topics have evidence. Overall research is partial because no complete videos could be played, the target of 40–80 full reviews was not met, and all ten direct watch-page requests throttled.

The sample is a free tracker’s selected long-form videos from 27 tracked channels plus its YouTube search. It has no census of the broader platform, Shorts or live formats. Ten videos from ten channels were retained.

YouTube views and likes are third-party counters measured at 15:01 Chicago on November 7. Comments, subscriber counts and sponsorship disclosures were unavailable for all retained videos. X publisher-post counts are separately timed third-party values; Hacker News displayed counts have an unknown index refresh time.
The six matches are program-level snapshot differences from the same tracker. Multi-topic video counts are not allocated to individual topics. Rank movement and global audience momentum are unknown.
top10.note: Report, source-readback and search receipts are separate observations. Snapshot binding verifies the collected report bytes; the consumed commit is independently corroborated only when the separately fetched source bytes match. These records do not independently attest scheduler identity or source truth. Top 10 reporting does not change Brief/image release status.
